structure.overview: This case concerns an appeal by appellants against a Federal Court order that affirmed an Associate Judge's dismissal of their late extension request to appeal a struck statement of claim. The appellants argued that the lower courts erred in their discretionary refusal to grant an extension of time, but the Federal Court of Appeal found no legal error and upheld the refusal. Consequently, the appeal was dismissed and costs were awarded to the respondents.

party_points.text: errors in assuming appeal merit without summary assessment

summaries.speaker: party
summaries.summary: Appellants argue errors in assuming appeal merit without summary assessment, no reasonable delay explanation, inferred respondent prejudice, and injustice in refusing extension.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court rejects appellants' arguments, upholding the assumption of some merit without full evaluation as proper under Hennelly and related cases.

citations.cite: LeBlanc v. National Bank of Canada, [1994] 1 F.C. 81 at p. 92 (F.C.)
citations.why: Supports assumption of some merit without full evaluation

citations.cite: Qualizza at para. 16
citations.why: Supports assumption of some merit without full evaluation

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court affirms the Federal Court's rejection of appellants' explanations for delay, finding no error or basis to intervene.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court agrees the long delay justifies concern for prejudice and supports denying extension in interests of justice, citing relevant precedents.
idea_list: delay length relevant to interests of justice

citations.cite: Larkman at para. 62
citations.why: Supports considering delay length in interests of justice

citations.cite: Gambler First Nation v. Ledoux, 2020 FCA 204 at para. 6

citations.cite: Larkman at paras. 86-88

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Court finds no error in the Federal Court's refusal of extension, rejecting appellants' reliance on Koch and affirming deference to factor weighing.

citations.cite: Koch v. Borgatti Estate, 2022 FCA 201
citations.why: Rejects appellants' claim that Koch changed test for extensions

citations.cite: Canada (Attorney General) v. Fontaine, 2017 SCC 47 at para. 36
citations.why: Supports deference to weighing of factors

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The appeal is dismissed and appellants must pay costs of $2,500 to each respondent as agreed by parties.
